blocks.title: Drones: Small Aircraft, Big Ideas
blocks.subtitle: How multirotors fly, sense, navigate and carry out a mission

blocks.text:
A drone is an aircraft without a pilot on board. It may be flown by a person on the ground, follow a pre-planned route, or make its own decisions from what its sensors report.

Cheap inertial sensors, satellite navigation, lithium batteries and brushless motors turned drones from military systems into everyday tools for farmers, surveyors, film-makers and scientists.

blocks.heading: How a quadcopter stays level
blocks.text: A quadcopter has no wings or tail. It controls itself entirely by changing the speed of its four propellers. Two spin clockwise and two anticlockwise so their torques cancel. Speeding up one pair tilts or turns the aircraft, and a flight controller makes these corrections hundreds of times a second.

steps.text: **Sense.** An inertial measurement unit reports rotation rates and accelerations. A barometer, magnetometer and GNSS receiver add height, heading and position.
**Estimate.** A filter fuses the noisy sensors into one best estimate of attitude, velocity and position.
**Control.** Control loops compare that estimate with what the pilot or mission asks for and compute the thrust each motor must produce.
**Act.** Electronic speed controllers switch battery power into the brushless motors to deliver exactly that thrust.

blocks.heading: Rules of the air
blocks.text: Because drones share airspace with crewed aircraft and fly over people, most countries regulate them by weight and by risk. Typical rules cover registration, pilot competency, maximum height, visual line of sight, and zones where flying is prohibited or needs permission. Always check the current rules of the country you fly in before a flight.

items.title: IMU
items.text: Gyroscopes and accelerometers on a chip: the sense of balance of every drone.

items.title: PID control
items.text: A simple, widely used control law that corrects error using its present value, its history and its rate of change.

items.title: RTK positioning
items.text: Corrections from a base station improve GNSS accuracy from metres to centimetres.

items.title: Return-to-home
items.text: A failsafe that flies the drone back to its launch point if the link or battery becomes critical.

items.title: BVLOS
items.text: Beyond visual line of sight: operations where the pilot cannot see the aircraft and must rely on systems.

items.title: Geofencing
items.text: Software limits that keep a drone out of restricted areas or inside a permitted volume.

blocks.heading: Open problems
blocks.text: Battery energy limits most small drones to well under an hour of flight. Safe operation beyond line of sight needs reliable detect-and-avoid and traffic management. Security matters too: command links can be jammed or spoofed, and misuse near airports and sensitive sites has driven work on counter-drone systems.

blocks.question: How does a quadcopter turn (yaw) without a tail rotor?
options: It speeds up the pair spinning one way and slows the other pair
blocks.explanation: Changing the balance between clockwise and anticlockwise rotors leaves a net torque that turns the aircraft.

blocks.question: What is the job of an electronic speed controller (ESC)?
options: Drive a brushless motor at the speed the flight controller commands
blocks.explanation: The ESC switches battery power through the motor windings to produce the commanded speed.

blocks.heading: Key terms and next steps
blocks.text:
**UAS**: unmanned aircraft system, the aircraft plus its ground equipment and links. **VLOS/BVLOS**: within or beyond visual line of sight. **Payload**: what the drone carries to do its job. **Failsafe**: automatic behaviour when something goes wrong.
